# Deferred-Anchor Registry — Harness

> The canonical source of truth for every `D-*` anchor cited in `src/` but
> deferred to a future cycle. The leading underscore sorts this file before
> the numbered plans in directory listings — call this out as the registry,
> not a plan. Per-plan §3.1 rows are still the preferred home for anchors
> whose feature area maps cleanly onto a plan; this file catches the orphans
> + cross-cutting anchors that don't belong to any single plan.
>
> **CI/pre-commit guard** (`scripts/check-anchor-registry/check-anchor-registry.{sh,ps1}`): every
> `D-*` identifier appearing in `src/` MUST resolve to a row in this file
> OR a citation in any `.plans/*.md`. Pre-fix this recurred TWICE
> (memory: "the same gap silent-failure caught for MULTI-PAGE-GOT").
> The guard makes the system enforce the discipline — same shape as the
> agnosticism veto + the `CallConv` static_assert.
>
> **★ ANCHOR-NAME RULE — READ BEFORE INVENTING A `D-*` NAME (documented 2026-07-28, TF-C81; it was
> load-bearing and unwritten until it bit).** The guard's regex is
> `D-[A-Z0-9_]+(-[A-Z0-9_]+){2,}` — **`D-` plus THREE OR MORE `-`-separated segments is a
> DEFERRED-WORK ANCHOR and MUST resolve to a row here; a TWO-segment `D-*` name (`D-OPT`) is an
> informal feature label the guard ignores.** So hyphenating a COMPOUND FEATURE WORD silently changes
> the identifier's CLASS: `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYS-INLINE` tripped the guard and had to be renamed
> `D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE` to match its sibling `D-CSUBSET-NOINLINE`. The failure surfaces as
> “missing row”, which misdirects you into WRITING a duplicate row instead of FIXING the name.
> **Spell a compound feature word as ONE segment (`ALWAYSINLINE`, `NOINLINE`); reserve hyphens for
> genuine name components; when in doubt, match the sibling anchor already in this file.** Full
> write-up: [[D-PLANS-ANCHOR-NAME-SEGMENT-COUNT-GATE]].
>
> **V2-4.X / full-C ownership (2026-06-10):** the C-language-feature deferral

> V2-4.X / [`23-full-c-plan`](./23-full-c-plan%20-%20tbd.md)** (c-subset → full

> **★★ MEASUREMENT CAVEAT — READ BEFORE QUOTING ANY “this will clear N errors” NUMBER IN THIS FILE (2026-07-28, macOS-arm64 predefine-probe cycle).** DSS **abandons a TU at its first hard parse failure**, so a corpus error count is a count of the errors REACHED, never of the defects PRESENT. Clearing an early blocker therefore EXPOSES later ones that were never reached, and a drop in the total is NOT a count of defects fixed. Worked example from this cycle: the 189-TU sqlite build went **213 → 80** total errors when architecture + toolchain predefines were both supplied — that is **NOT 133 defects fixed**; the residual 80 is a NEWLY-EXPOSED population whose composition was unknown until separately measured. It is equally possible for a real fix to make the total go UP (this cycle measured exactly that: toolchain-identity macros ALONE took 213 → 216). Every forward estimate of the form “closing X clears N errors” in any row below MUST be read with this caveat, and every new one MUST carry it. See [[D-MEASURE-FIRST-FAILURE-MASKS-RESIDUAL]] for the citable class row.

> ⚠⚠ **THIS REGISTRY IS ONE OF TWO. IT HOLDS HARNESS ROWS ONLY (574 of them).**
> Its sibling is [`_deferred-anchor-registry-production.md`](_deferred-anchor-registry-production.md) (1357 rows).
> Split 2026-08-25 on operator instruction: *"2 deferred anchor registry files, one for prod,
> other for tool/harness ... the priority is real errors, not cosmetics"* — one pile of 1890 rows
> made the compiler defects unreadable underneath the test and gate defects.
>
> **THE LINE BETWEEN THEM, so a borderline row is decided by a rule and not by taste:**
> **PRODUCTION** is a defect a USER OF THE COMPILER could hit — it is in the shipped binary or in
> the config that binary reads (front end, preprocessor, semantics, HIR/MIR/LIR, optimiser,
> assembler, linker, object formats, FFI surface, diagnostics, CLI, emitted runtime).
> **HARNESS** is a defect only WE can hit — tests, gates, guards, the cycle machinery, plans,
> scripts, carriages, CI, the example corpus AS a corpus.
> ⚠ `D-CONFIG-*` and `D-DIAG-*` are PRODUCTION deliberately: a `.lang/.target/.format.json`
> document IS the compiler's behaviour in this architecture, and a diagnostic is its output to a
> user. Filing either as tooling would hide real conformance defects in the harness pile, which is
> the exact thing this split exists to stop.
> ⚠ A row's bucket follows the DEFECT, never the instrument that found it: a corpus example that
> reveals a codegen bug files under codegen.
>
> ★ **EVERY CONSUMER GLOBS `_deferred-anchor-registry*.md`** rather than naming two paths, so a
> future third split costs nothing and no reader can silently see only half the registry.

## Anchor Index

**Row shape: EXACTLY four cells — `Anchor`, `Trigger`, `Closing work`, `Cross-refs`.**
A row with fewer cells shifts every following cell one column LEFT; a row with more
has the surplus SILENTLY DROPPED by the renderer. Neither is visible when reading the
raw text, so the count is load-bearing — see `D-PLANS-REGISTRY-MALFORMED-ROW-CELLS`.

Two authoring rules follow from that, both verified against the GitHub renderer:
- **A raw `|` splits a cell EVEN INSIDE BACKTICKS.** To quote an expression, regex or
  alternation containing one, write `\|` — the backslash-escaped form is the *only*
  one that survives inside a code span (an HTML entity does **not**).
- **` ═══ ` inside a cell marks a seam where two cells were joined** when a row
  authored to a wider schema was converged onto these four columns. It is a joint in
  the prose, not a column boundary.

⚠ **APPEND AT END-OF-TABLE, NEVER AT END-OF-FILE.** This registry once carried a
second `## Anchor Index (continued)` table, which existed only because rows had been
appended past the Allowlist over many cycles; its header declared TWO columns, so every
fuller row silently lost its `Closing work` and `Cross-refs`. The 2026-08-25
production/harness split merged both tables, so each file now has exactly ONE index and
the accident cannot recur here -- but the rule that prevents it still has to be obeyed.

| `D-TEST-ARM64-TCL-CROSSBUILD-BIGNUM-HARNESS-CONFOUND` | **✅ CLOSED 2026-07-24 (found + fixed during the arm64 `veryquick` corpus run) — the arm64 test HARNESS's cross-built Tcl had broken int64→bignum promotion, manufacturing FALSE "DSS failures". DSS was never involved.** Symptom: `orderby9-1.0/1.1` failed on arm64 (`expected [1] got [0]`) while the x86_64 baseline passed them. Discrimination chain, in order: (1) a SQL-level probe on the arm64 DSS shell was CORRECT — bigint `ORDER BY` properly ascending AND `SELECT random() AS y FROM t1 ORDER BY 1` came back SORTED; (2) a TCL probe showed the list sqlite returned had **0 descents** (i.e. genuinely sorted) and it was `lsort -command bigintcompare` that reordered it; (3) `bigintcompare` is `expr {$a-$b}`, which OVERFLOWS int64 on the extremes (−9.2e18 − 3.3e18 ≈ −1.25e19) and so exercises Tcl's bignum promotion — a path living entirely in gcc-built `libtcl8.6.a`; (4) **decisive**: a PURE gcc `tclsh8.6` with ZERO DSS code linked showed `expr {9223372036854775807 + 1}` = `-9223372036854775808` (wrapped) on arm64 vs the correct `9223372036854775808` on the x86_64 system tclsh, while explicit `entier(1)<<70` was correct in both (so libtommath was fine — only AUTOMATIC overflow promotion was broken). ROOT: the original `build_tcl.sh` passed `--host=aarch64-linux-gnu --build=x86_64-linux-gnu`, which makes autoconf treat the build as CROSS and **skip every `AC_RUN_IFELSE` probe**, taking hand-fed cache answers instead (`tcl_cv_type_64bit='long int'`, `tcl_cv_strtod_buggy=ok`, `tcl_cv_strtod_unbroken=ok`, `ac_cv_func_strtod=yes`). One of those guesses is wrong for this target, and Tcl compiled an inconsistent 64-bit arithmetic path. **FIX:** `qemu-aarch64` binfmt_misc IS registered on this host, so configure can EXECUTE target binaries — rebuild with the cross compiler but WITHOUT `--host`/`--build`, letting every probe run for real (`checking for 64-bit integer type... using long`). Result: pure tclsh `max+1` correct, and `orderby9.test` → **0 errors out of 5 tests** with the DSS-compiled objects **BYTE-IDENTICAL** (same `tf_arm88/o/*.o`, relinked only). ★★ **LESSON (the reason this is anchored rather than left as folklore): a cross-built test HARNESS is itself a confound, and a canned autoconf cache is a silent-wrong-answer machine. Before attributing ANY corpus failure to the compiler, check whether the failing assertion runs through harness code — here the whole failure lived in `expr`/`lsort`, not in a single line of DSS output.** ★ Two of my own hypotheses were REFUTED by experiment before the real cause was found (that gcc `-O2` deleted a UB overflow check — `-fwrapv` changed nothing, and Tcl's `Overflowing()` is pure bit logic, not UB; and that the sort or double-evaluation of `random()` was wrong — both were fine). | ✅ (CLOSED) | arm64 corpus arc (2026-07-24); harness only — NO repo source change (the recipe lives in `scratchpad/build_tcl.sh` + the memory topic file, both corrected); canonical arm64 Tcl is now the binfmt-probed build; pairs with the known non-DSS `walsetlk`/`busy2` wall-clock-timing class (amplified under qemu). |

| `D-TEST-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-PARALLEL-CONTENTION-FLAKE` | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-07-24 (TF-C58 gate — trigger FIRED: it red-ed 3 of 4 consecutive full Win ctest runs, a different example each time). ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is NOT the spawn-timeout fragility this row hypothesized.** The real mechanism is a `ScratchDir` PATH COLLISION (`tests/test_support/scratch_dir.hpp`, shared by every test that needs a scratch dir). The ctor built `<base>/<pid>-<counter>` and called `create_directories`, checking only `ec` and IGNORING the return value — and `create_directories` reports SUCCESS when the directory ALREADY EXISTS. The dtor's `remove_all` swallowed its `ec`, so directories leak whenever a spawned example binary still holds a handle or a run is killed (**55** were sitting in `test-scratch/examples/` when this was found). A process drawing a recycled PID (Windows reuses them freely) plus the same counter value therefore SILENTLY SHARED a stale directory, and the runner's next `copy_file` — which does not pass `overwrite_existing` — threw `filesystem error: cannot copy file: File exists [.../main.c]`. That explains every observed symptom the timeout theory could not: it hits a DIFFERENT example each run, it reproduces in SERIAL runs too (`-j1`, via PID reuse against leaked dirs, not concurrency), it passes on isolated re-run, and it worsens the longer a working tree goes without cleaning `test-scratch/`. **FIX (one chokepoint — both runners and every other ScratchDir consumer inherit it):** the ctor now LOOPS on `create_directory` (singular) and accepts only a slot whose creation it actually won, which is atomic in the OS and therefore race-free across concurrent `ctest -j` processes as well as stale-dir-safe; a bounded attempt cap fails loud naming the accumulation; and the dtor now WARNS on stderr instead of silently swallowing a failed `remove_all`, so leakage is visible while still small. WITNESS: `test_scratch_dir.cpp::StaleDirectoryOnTheNextSlotIsNotReused` plants a populated directory on the exact slot the ctor will draw next (predicted from a probe ScratchDir's own filename, so it pins real ctor behaviour) — **red-on-disable DEMONSTRATED: restoring the return-value-ignoring `create_directories` fails BOTH expectations, while the pre-existing `MultipleScratchDirsGetDistinctPaths` stays GREEN** (it advances the counter either way — an inert pin that was green through the entire lifetime of the bug, the §A.5 trap). Post-fix: full Win ctest green. ★ NOTE the spawn-timeout hypothesis recorded below was never confirmed; if example flakes recur after this, re-open on that theory with fresh evidence rather than assuming it. **_(Original entry retained below.)_** ⏳ was OPEN, trigger-gated -- named 2026-07-23 (TF-C54 gate; recurring since >=TF-C51).** Under a PARALLEL full `ctest -j4` on the Windows leg, examples-runner entries (each spawns a compiled example subprocess with a 5s timeout) intermittently FAIL on load-timing -- distinct entries each occurrence (TF-C51: 2; the TF-C54 iterations: `deep_expr_lower`, then `bare_int_condition`, then 4-at-once right after a WSL-gate teardown), EVERY one passing on an ISOLATED re-run, and the same tree 727/727 on the WSL leg. NOT a product defect (the examples are EXEC-path front-end/codegen witnesses; the flaking set is uncorrelated with the diff under test) -- a HARNESS timing fragility: subprocess spawn + 5s wall-clock timeout under heavy parallel load. Operational protocol (memory + skill): run the Win ctest ALONE (never concurrent with a WSL gate) + re-run any examples fail ISOLATED to discriminate flake-vs-regression. This row makes the recurring pattern REGISTRY-VISIBLE (§A.7) instead of per-cycle folklore. Trigger: a CI leg (which runs examples serially today) starts hitting it, OR the local flake rate materially disrupts gates. Closing work: make the runner robust under parallel load -- e.g. a load-scaled/generous spawn timeout, ctest RESOURCE_LOCK/serialization for examples entries, or a retry-once-with-loud-tag arm (design choice at closure; a silent auto-retry that could mask a REAL intermittent regression is NOT acceptable per §A.4). | Make examples-runner ctest entries robust under parallel load (today: run alone + isolated re-run protocol). | `tests/examples/examples_runner.cpp` + `integrated_tests/runner.cpp` (the two runners); [[D-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-CLI-SUBPROCESS-NESTED-DEPENDSON]] (where the 5s-timeout masking bit before); the dss-cycle/memory operational protocol; ★ **2026-08-04 POINTER ADDED — the "run alone (never concurrent with a WSL gate)" protocol quoted in this row is SUPERSEDED and must not be re-derived from here:** it was refuted by measurement at TF-C105 (concurrent Windows ctest + WSL gate + agents rebuilding `build-dbg` → 771/771, exit 0) and the surviving, mechanism-specific rule is [[D-GATE-SHARED-DLL-RELINK-UNDER-RUNNING-CTEST]] — concurrency is fine, relinking the shared DLL underneath a running ctest is not |

TWO corpus examples pin the [[D-TARGET-CHAR-SIGNEDNESS-PER-PLATFORM]] miscompile as correct — `examples/c/char_signedness/expected.json` (macho row asserts **20**, should be **10**) and `examples/c/char_value/expected.json` (ctest #294, macho row asserts **131**, should be **132** — clang native measures 132) — and `char_value/main.c:26-28` argues the wrong value is right IN PROSE. ★ **THE FAILURE MODE IS THE REPAIR, NOT THE BUG:** the cycle that finally corrects the descriptor will see **two RED examples** and the path of least resistance — especially under a green-suite ratchet — is to “fix the tests”, restoring the defective expectations and re-cementing the bug **with the suite as evidence that it is correct**. ★★ **THE RULES: (i)** when a row records that an expectation is WRONG, name the exact files, rows and both numbers in the anchor, so the repairing cycle meets the warning before it meets the red; **(ii)** annotate the assertion IN PLACE, next to the number, not only in the registry — the person editing it is looking at the file, not at `.plans/`; **(iii)** these examples may be **flipped, never deleted or relaxed** — deleting them destroys the only per-target signedness witness, and relaxing them (dropping the per-target row) silently re-admits BOTH answers; **(iv)** treat “a test went red while I was fixing a config bug” as evidence to CHECK THE TEST, not automatically to fix the code. ★ ROOT CAUSE worth noting: both examples inherited the false claim from ONE source — the `$charIsUnsignedComment` at `src/dss-config/targets/arm64.target.json:14` — so a single wrong sentence in a config comment became three wrong assertions. **A config comment stating an ABI fact is load-bearing documentation; a wrong one is copied forward by everyone who trusts it.** ⭐⭐⭐⭐ **SPECIES (6) — THE BARE `ASSERT_FALSE`: A TEST THAT CANNOT TELL YOU *WHICH GUARD FIRED*. Added 2026-07-28 (TF-C76), WITH A MEASUREMENT, and it is the cheapest species to create by accident.** `ObjectFormatSchemaLoader.UnknownSentinelKindRejectedByValidate` was, at baseline `657c3a9`, a single `ASSERT_FALSE(r.has_value())` over a fixture JSON — it asserted only that **the load failed**, not that it failed **for the stated reason**. Such a fixture is one unrelated typo away (a misspelled `dataModel`, a malformed `relocations`) from staying GREEN forever while the property it names goes unguarded. ★★ **THE MEASURED PROOF THAT THIS IS NOT THEORETICAL — and it is a cleaner demonstration than species (4)'s, because BOTH guards are correct and both are wanted:** TF-C76 added a second, independent rejection of the sentinel at the JSON LOAD SITE. **With that new load-site guard disabled, the bare-`ASSERT_FALSE` test STILL PASSED** — because `validate()` catches the sentinel further down and the load still fails — and **only the message-content assertion went red.** A boolean "did it fail?" cannot distinguish two guards; it is satisfied by any failure at all, including failures that have nothing to do with the test's name. ★ **THE RULE: a fail-loud pin must assert the diagnostic's CODE and PATH and that its MESSAGE names the offending thing — never merely that the operation failed.** Strengthened in place ✔TREE `tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp` (`UnknownSentinelKindRejectedByValidate` now scans for `/format/kind` + `C_MalformedJson` + a message naming the sentinel), and a second witness `SentinelKindDoesNotCascadeIntoIdentityBlockNoise` pins the cascade-elimination half. ⚠ **NOTE WHAT IS *NOT* CLAIMED: no diagnostic COUNT is asserted in either** — the property is "the rejection names the kind" and "no per-block advice rides along", both expressible without predicting how many diagnostics the loader emits ([[D-PLANS-ANCHOR-EXPECTATION-BECOMES-SPEC]] rule (iii)). ⭐ **AND A TEST-TALLY WARNING THAT BELONGS WHEREVER TEST-COUNT EXPECTATIONS ARE RECORDED: ctest counts BINARIES, NOT gtest CASES.** TF-C76 landed **14 new gtest cases** and ctest stayed at **728/728** — ✔TREE-verified (`ctest -N` reports `Total Tests: 728`; the cycle's `tests/` diff adds 14 new `TEST(` fixtures). CMake registers roughly one ctest entry per test EXECUTABLE (plus the per-example corpus entries), so adding cases to an existing binary moves the ctest tally by ZERO. **Anyone reading an unchanged ctest tally as evidence that no coverage was added — or reading a changed one as a coverage delta — is misled in both directions.** Use the gtest case count for coverage, the ctest tally for suite health. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **SPECIES (7) — THE WARNING THAT WAS WRITTEN, PUBLISHED, AND STILL DID NOT PREVENT THE TRAP. Added 2026-07-28 (TF-C77). ★ This species is not about a test at all; it is evidence about WHERE a warning has to LIVE to work.** The trap itself is the documented one: an over-aligned global needs an OFFSET BREAKER in front of it, because the first over-aligned global in a section lands at the section start and every object format page-aligns those — so `&av % 64 == 0` holds whether or not the alignment sink ran, and the check is VACUOUS BY PLACEMENT. ✔TREE it was already written down, in bold, with a measured before/after matrix, in a NEIGHBOURING example: `examples/c/gnu_aligned_attribute/main.c` ("★★ THE OFFSET BREAKERS (`bss_pad`, `data_pad`) ARE LOAD-BEARING", plus a three-row `★ VACUOUS` table and the `.bss`-vs-`.data` section-class rule at `:46-47`). **It did not work.** The TF-C77 implementer, authoring `examples/c/gnu_attribute_mid_position_crosscu/`, reached for a breaker — and reached for the WRONG ONE: an UNINITIALIZED `char pad;` (`.bss`) in front of an INITIALIZED `av` (`.data`). MEASURED: the alignment check still returned 42 under the H1 slot-off disable, i.e. VACUOUS, the exact failure the neighbouring file names in bold. They caught it themselves (the H1 column is what exposed it), switched to an initialized `data_pad = 1` in the SAME section class, and RE-MEASURED 42 → 1 under H1. ★★ **THE FINDING IS THE FAILURE OF THE WARNING, NOT THE FAILURE OF THE AUTHOR** — the warning was correct, prominent, recent, and in a sibling directory of the file being written, and it was still not consulted at the moment of the mistake. **A warning that lives in a neighbouring example is read only by someone who already suspects the problem.** The half that transferred was "there must be a breaker"; the half that did not was "it must be the SAME SECTION CLASS as the object it precedes" — the half that is actually load-bearing. **THE RULES: (i)** a trap of this shape needs the warning where the MISTAKE is made, not where it was first discovered — beside the declaration, in the row that the closing work reads, or (best) enforced; **(ii)** the only reason this one was caught is that the disable matrix was run PER CHECK against the FINAL build and its column was READ — a whole-file revert would have hidden it, and so would running the matrix and only checking that "something went red"; **(iii)** treat "my non-vacuity probe came back green" as a RESULT TO EXPLAIN, not as a pass. ★ This is the second time the same physical trap has been paid for; a third occurrence is the trigger to make it mechanical (a runner check that an over-aligned global in a corpus example is preceded by a same-section-class object) rather than to write the warning a third time. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **SPECIES (8) — THE BYTE-EQUALITY ROUND-TRIP: A TEST THAT COMPARES TWO COPIES OF THE SAME BLIND SPOT. Added 2026-07-28 (TF-C78), MEASURED.** ✔TREE `tests/mir/test_mir_text.cpp:36`'s `roundTrip` helper asserts `emit → parse → emit` **byte-equality** and is used by eight cases. It could **never** have caught that `mir_text.cpp` was dropping a function's `binding` AND `visibility`: the printer emitted no attribute list, the parser called the 2-argument `addFunction` and re-minted every function as `(Global, Default)` — so a `static` function round-tripped as externally visible and a `weak` one as strong — and **both emits omitted the field, so both matched and the suite stayed green** through every cycle that touched the file. ★★ **THE RULE, and it generalises past MIR text to every serializer, printer, pretty-printer and golden-text pin in the tree: A ROUND-TRIP TEST IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE EMITTER'S COMPLETENESS. Byte-equality over `emit∘parse∘emit` is structurally incapable of detecting a field that NEITHER SIDE WRITES — it proves the two emits agree, not that either is faithful.** The fix shape is the reusable part: the replacement pins (`MirText.FunctionAttributesSurviveRoundTrip`) read the **PARSED MODULE's accessors** (`parsed->mir.funcBinding/funcVisibility/funcNoInline`) directly rather than comparing text — the only formulation that can observe a dropped field — plus an all-default function pinning the other direction (the attribute list must be OMITTED when nothing is set, so an unconditional emit that would churn every existing golden is caught too). ★ **SCOPE, so this is not inflated:** `parseMir` has **no `src/` callers** (✔TREE MEASURED — definition, declaration and two doc comments only; the callers are two test files), so this was a **TEST-SUBSTRATE** defect, never a live miscompile. That is why it belongs in THIS row and not among the miscompile rows. ★ **WHAT IS STILL OPEN AT THE SAME SITE:** the per-GLOBAL half — `parseGlobal` re-mints `binding`, `visibility`, `isConst`, `isThreadLocal` and `alignment` — see [[D-MIRTEXT-GLOBAL-FLAGS-DROPPED-BY-ROUNDTRIP]]. **The vacuity argument above applies to it unchanged, so do not "verify" it with the `roundTrip` helper.** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **SPECIES (9) — THE GUARD TESTED ONLY THROUGH A PATH WHERE A *DIFFERENT MECHANISM* ALREADY PRODUCES THE ASSERTED OUTCOME. Enumerate the routes before believing a guard is covered — the same counting discipline [[D-CSUBSET-ALWAYSINLINE]] arrived at from the other direction ("count how many times the pipeline RE-CONSULTS a flag before concluding a hop needs no pin").** ★ TWO FURTHER SHAPES, TF-C88 (fc0908d), both found in the cycle's OWN FRESH TESTS and only because each arm was disabled ALONE: (i) a CONTAINMENT check on a name a defect would PREFIX is structurally incapable of seeing that defect — asserting merely that `dss_c88_single` is FOUND passes under a double-mangle, because `_dss_c88_single` CONTAINS it; the arm became real only once it ALSO asserted the mangled form ABSENT, i.e. TWO-SIDED. MEASURED: BSD sed extracts **0** lines with `\?` vs **52** with the POSIX form; GNU sed extracts **52 either way** — so the fix `\(local \)*` (`\(...\)` + `*` are both core POSIX BRE, no `-E`, no dialect dependency) leaves the Linux/Windows legs BYTE-UNCHANGED. `*` still matches the `local`-prefixed form, preserving the deliberate extract-then-fail-at-runtime design of the sibling anchor. **(2) `bash` resolved via PATH, not the running interpreter (the root cause).** `build-and-test.sh` re-execs itself into bash 4+ (line 67), then invoked the self-test as a bare `bash "$_selftest"` — PATH bash on macOS is **/bin/bash 3.2**, which has no `declare -A`. Instrument (b) cannot be a scheduling or fork artifact: both reads happen in one process microseconds apart. ★★ **CONFIRMED AT SCALE the same day:** the sampler ran for the WHOLE **7 h 45 m** `full`-tier harness run — **13,932 samples, 1,108 steps >\|0.1 s\|, max +34.970 s / min −34.970 s**. Its message was `NATIVE-PROBE-COMPILE-FAILED … Failing step: build command \`""…\\build_probe.bat""\`` — which names the command and nothing else, because `runNativeCProbe` called `std::system(build.c_str())` with **both streams discarded**. A compiler explains itself on stderr; that explanation went nowhere, so a one-shot failure was undiagnosable at the moment it mattered. ★ **THE IRONY IS THE POINT AND IS WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A NICETY:** this file exists BECAUSE a probe once conflated "no compiler installed" with "a step broke", and its whole design is about keeping statuses apart — `ToolAbsent` vs `ToolQueryFailed` vs `CompileFailed` vs `ExecutableMissing` vs `RunFailed` vs `OutputUnreadable` vs `EmptyOutput`. It distinguishes WHICH step broke meticulously and then drops WHY for the one step that can say. **FIX, IN TWO PARTS — AND THE SECOND WAS ONLY FOUND BY EXERCISING THE FIRST:** (1) a `captureCmd()` sibling to the existing `redirectCmd()` — it appends `> log 2>&1` to an ALREADY-ASSEMBLED command line instead of quoting a path (quoting the vcvars `&&` chain again would corrupt it), keeping cmd.exe's outer-quote rule for the same reason `redirectCmd` keeps it — plus `tailOf()`, which folds the last 30 lines into the detail and keeps **unreadable / empty / present** as three distinct answers rather than collapsing them to `""`. `build.empty()` stays FIRST in the `\|\|` so `captureCmd` is never handed an empty command. ★★ (2) **THE MSVC BATCH WAS SILENCING `cl` ITSELF.** The generated `build_probe.bat` ended its compile line with `>nul 2>&1`, so the capture collected an EMPTY log and reported "the build command produced NO output at all" — ✔which is precisely what it said the first time the arm was exercised. The capture was correct and was pointed at a stream already emptied one level down. `cl`'s silencer is removed; `call vcvars` keeps its own, because on success it prints a pure-noise banner and its failure is already covered upstream by `locateMsvcToolchain`. ⓘ **THAT ORDERING IS THE LESSON:** part (1) alone would have shipped looking finished, and its output — the honest string "NO output at all" — would have been read as "the compiler said nothing", which is false. Only running the failure arm distinguished them. ✔**DEMONSTRATED END-TO-END:** with a deliberate syntax error injected into the emitted `probe.c`, the message now carries `probe.c(3): error C2018: character 'U+40' is not permitted here` and eight more lines, file and line included; mutation reverted byte-identical (sha256) and both ABI witnesses re-run green. ⚠ **THE RISK IS SHELL QUOTING AND IT IS LOUD, NOT SILENT:** get it wrong and the build fails on every host and every run — checked on Windows (cmd.exe) and under WSL (POSIX sh) both. That is the opposite of the failure mode this file warns about, where a wrong redirection SILENTLY became "no compiler installed". ★ **THE ONE-SHOT FAILURE THAT EXPOSED THIS IS A SEPARATE, STILL-OPEN QUESTION — see [[D-TEST-NATIVE-PROBE-COMPILE-FAILS-UNDER-CONCURRENT-LOAD]].** This row closes the DIAGNOSTIC gap only; it does not explain the failure, and must not be read as having done so. | Cross-refs: `tests/core/native_c_probe.hpp` (`captureCmd`, `tailOf`, and the capture at the CompileFailed arm) · `tests/core/test_packed_abi_conformance.cpp` (the witness that hit it) · [[D-TEST-FIXED-SCRATCH-PATH-POPULATION]] (ruled OUT as the cause here: `ScratchDir` claims its directory atomically with `create_directory`, so a collision is excluded by construction) |

The fix is mostly WIRING AN EXISTING SIGNAL INTO THE RIGHT PLACE, not new machinery. **(b) DELETE the marker, rc and log at the START of a run**, so an in-flight run has NO marker at all and a premature read finds nothing instead of something wrong. **(c) PREFER PER-RUN PATHS OUTRIGHT** — a marker whose path encodes its run cannot be mistaken for another's, which removes the class rather than detecting it. Once the installed root exists it is AUTHORITATIVE — a miss inside it STOPS the search rather than falling through, because mixing two config trees in one compilation is a silent wrongness of its own. The relative hop is **COMPUTED BY CMAKE** from the same `GNUInstallDirs` variables the `install()` rules use and forwarded as `DSS_INSTALL_CONFIG_RELDIR` (`#error` if absent), so the install set and the lookup cannot disagree about where the tree lives; an absolute `CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR`/`DATADIR` is a configure-time `FATAL_ERROR` because it would make the package non-relocatable. Executable path comes from the KERNEL (`GetModuleFileNameW`/`_NSGetExecutablePath`/`/proc/self/exe`), NEVER `argv[0]`. A not-found now LISTS EVERY PATH TRIED. ⚠ **ONE STATED NARROWING, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug:** the DIRECTORY form returns `std::optional`, so a skewed tree and a genuine miss are the same answer there — the skew EXPLANATION comes from the file form, which every compilation reaches first (the driver resolves the language schema before any directory lookup). Widening that signature would ripple into four files owned by concurrent work, and correctness holds either way because both forms run the SAME precedence, so a skewed tree is never USED and the two can never read different trees. **(3) SKEW FAILS LOUD** — the installed path carries the binary's OWN version segment (`share/dss-code-prime/<version>/dss-config`, gcc's `/usr/lib/gcc/<triple>/<ver>/` answer), so on that arm skew is **UNREPRESENTABLE** rather than merely detectable — a newer binary dropped over an older install fails loud instead of silently compiling against old descriptors; the two repo-shaped arms read the tree's own `VERSION` and REFUSE a mismatch naming both versions and the tree. ⚠ **RC'S BUILD STAMP WAS DELIBERATELY *NOT* REUSED, and its own header says why**: the stamp is maximally sensitive BY DESIGN (commit + dirty-content digest) because a cache key must over-invalidate, whereas a compatibility check must be exactly as sensitive as the compatibility boundary — reusing it would red every dirty dev build; its docblock also forbids a second includer, and `config_path_walk.cpp` lives in `core`, which would rebuild the world on every keystroke. **Both root on the SAME single owner** (the repo-root `VERSION` file), so this is one fact with two derived uses, not two owners. **VERIFIED — 4-mutant red-on-disable, five fail-closed clauses PLUS the mirror, every transition carrying an artifact-hash witness** (a PE relink changes the image even for identical source, so *changed* is the criterion, never *restored-to-baseline*): (A) the installed arm never resolves → RED; (B) the arm block MOVED below the cwd walk — a block move, so the ORDER claim is isolated from the EXISTENCE claim → RED; (C) the skew refusal removed → RED; (D) `install(DIRECTORY)` deleted → RED. ★★ **THE RED-ON-DISABLE CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT IN THE FIX ITSELF, and it is this cycle's lesson**: mutant A first came back **GREEN over a live mutant** because `installedConfigRootFrom` read the `DSS_INSTALL_CONFIG_RELDIR` macro DIRECTLY while the accessor `installedConfigRelDir()` read it separately — **two readers of one fact**, and the round-trip unit pin composed its expected path through the accessor, so the test was proving something about a path the implementation did not use. Collapsed to one reader; the mutant then went red. **Closing test — `install_scratch_prefix_smoke`** (a bare `add_test`, NOT `dss_add_test`, because the latter sets `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` and the test would then measure the override): installs to a scratch prefix under the system temp dir and compiles **and RUNS** a hello-world (`#include <stdio.h>`, exit 42, asserted stdout). ★★★ **THE SOURCE TREE BEING OUT OF REACH IS ENFORCED, NOT HOPED**: every ancestor of the scratch cwd is asserted free of `src/dss-config` **to the filesystem root** (further than the resolver's 8-hop bound), `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` is unset and re-asserted, and — the measurement rather than the argument — **THREE NEGATIVE CONTROLS**: with the installed tree renamed away the same compile MUST fail (if it did not, the green run was reading config from somewhere else) and MUST list the paths it tried; with a FULL COPY of the config tree planted in the cwd ancestry carrying a foreign `VERSION` the installed tree must still win (an EMPTY decoy would prove nothing — the probe would miss it either way); and that same tree named through `DSS_CONFIG_ROOT` must be REFUSED as skew naming both versions. The installed-vs-source file comparison is a **TOTAL set comparison against `src/dss-config/`**, never a list written in the test — ✔the first draft DID hand-list files and named one that exists only in a work-in-progress tree. Same total comparison guards the release leg in `pipeline-pkg.yml` (which now stages `cmake --install` and tars the PREFIX TREE, since `DSS_BUILD_TESTS=OFF` there means the ctest entry does not run). ⚠ **THE WARM `dist/release/` CACHE IS DELIBERATELY *NOT* INSTALLED AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN SILENT**: ✔MEASURED that the content-hashed object cache did not exist when this landed, so nothing produces `dist/` and an `install(DIRECTORY)` aimed at it would create an empty destination and report success — the vacuous-fix shape, reading for months as though the warm cache were shipping. That is the failure class the sibling `compile-bench` refuses BY NAME — it prints every reference it did NOT measure, with the probe that failed, on the stated grounds that *"a benchmark that quietly drops a compiler reads exactly like one where that compiler was fast"* — and this benchmark, published in `README.md` as the project's head-to-head against the reference compilers, did not. **THE FIX:** every reference found becomes its OWN `unix-cc` arm keyed on its own name; `--cc <path>` still pins exactly one, which is what a caller comparing against one specific build wants. ⓘ Two names resolving to ONE binary (macOS answers `gcc` with Apple clang) are deduped on the RESOLVED target and the skip is ANNOUNCED, because publishing two rows for one compiler invites the reader to compare them against each other. ★ **THE MEASUREMENT CORE NEEDED NO CHANGE AT ALL** — `speedtest1_bench.py` dispatches on `kind` and keys every record on `arm["id"]`, so N reference arms cost it nothing; ✔VERIFIED nothing anywhere depended on the literal arm id `"cc"`. The records cross the shell→python boundary as TSV rather than as JSON in an env var: a vendor version string is arbitrary text, and quoting it through a shell into JSON is the trap class this repository keeps paying for. **CONTEXT:** raised by the operator, 2026-08-25 — *"in linux/macos also the sqlite's speedtest1 but gcc and clang compile/execute time"* — which is why the gap was looked for at all. ✔VERIFIED by derivation on Windows: the emitted plan carries `dss` + `gcc 13.2.0` + `msvc`, arm ids `gcc`/`msvc` rather than the old `cc`. | ✅ CLOSED — one arm per reference compiler found, deduped by resolved target, skips announced | P35 fold; `real-examples/c/sqlite/benchmark-speedtest1.sh` (reference discovery + plan arms); same class as `scripts/compile-bench/`'s ABSENT/UNUSABLE table |
| D-HARNESS-SPEEDTEST1-BENCH-ASKS-make-FOR-A-TARGET-SPELLED-THE-POSIX-WAY | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-25 (cycle P35, fold) — the benchmark asked make to build `sqlite3d` while upstream declares the target as `sqlite3d$(T.exe)`, so on Windows it matched NO RULE and make answered `Nothing to be done for 'sqlite3d'` WITH EXIT STATUS 0 AND AN EMPTY RECIPE.** ✔MEASURED on this host: `make -B -n sqlite3d` emitted **0** compile lines where `make -B -n sqlite3d.exe` emitted **111**. ⚠ **IT FAILS IN THE SHAPE THAT COSTS THE MOST — not an error, an EMPTY ANSWER.** The TU floor then refused, which is the floor working, but the visible message was *"the full-source recipe derivation FAILED"* with **no cause named**, so the symptom pointed at the recipe PARSER while the defect was in the target NAME one layer above it. ★★★ **THIS IS A RECURRENCE OF AN ALREADY-ANCHORED CLASS:** [[D-HARNESS-FIXTURE-PATH-ASSUMES-THE-POSIX-ARTIFACT-SPELLING]], whose own headline in `base-harness.sh` reads *"WHAT DID THE COMPILER ACTUALLY WRITE? ASK IT, DO NOT GUESS."* That row removed the guess from the ARTIFACT spelling by making the compiler report what it committed — and the identical guess survived one layer up in the MAKE TARGET, where the authority is `make` and the question had simply never been asked. **THE FIX ASKS:** a command-line `--eval` target prints `$(T.exe)` from the very Makefile the build will use, and the answer is used for BOTH the reference build and the recipe derivation. ⛔ NO SUFFIX TABLE IS ADDED HERE — a third copy of that table is precisely what the anchored row was filed against. ✔VERIFIED by execution: `make target: sqlite3d.exe (T.exe='.exe', asked of make, not assumed)` then `recipe: sqlite3d.exe: 103 TUs, 30 defines, 6 -I dirs`, and the full derivation now completes `missing=0`. ⓘ A SECOND, SEPARATE trap was hit while proving this and is recorded rather than fixed: passing `--sqlite-dir` an MSYS path (`/c/Source/sqlite`) makes the manifest generator report `MISSING SOURCE` for **files that exist**, because the recipe's own paths are Windows-spelled. The native spelling works; the diagnostic is misleading and is a candidate for the same ask-do-not-guess treatment. | ✅ CLOSED — the make target carries the suffix make itself reports; derivation completes 103/103 | P35 fold; `real-examples/c/sqlite/benchmark-speedtest1.sh` (`CLI_TARGET`); recurrence of [[D-HARNESS-FIXTURE-PATH-ASSUMES-THE-POSIX-ARTIFACT-SPELLING]] |

## Allowlist (code-internal pins, NOT deferred work)

Anchor-shaped strings **in any root the guard scans** that are **not**
deferred-work markers and should be **ignored** by the CI guard. Add a row
when an in-code constant, a diagnostic-message identifier, or a purely
test-local pin matches the `D-*` regex but isn't a deferred-work anchor.

⚠ **THE SCOPE SENTENCE ABOVE SAID "in `src/`" UNTIL 2026-08-14 (AP6 Lane G2), AND
THAT WAS THE STALE HALF OF THIS SECTION, NOT A COSMETIC ONE.** The guard's roots
are `src/`, `examples/`, `tests/`, `integrated_tests/` and `real-examples/`
(`scripts/check-anchor-registry/check-anchor-registry.sh` `_ROOT_SPECS`, `.ps1` `$RootSpecs` — one table
per driver, per-root floors, and the two MUST stay byte-comparable). Written as
`src/`-only, the preamble read as a REFUSAL to allowlist a test-side pin, which
is exactly the class the AP6 widening surfaced en masse — so the sentence would
have pushed seven honest test-local pins toward fake registry rows. ⓘ The
`Pattern` column is matched by the same substring resolve every other `.plans/`
citation uses: there is **no separate allowlist parser** in either driver, so a
row here resolves its name by BEING here. ⚠ That means an entry is a real
decision with real reach — it silences the name everywhere, permanently. Do not
add one to quiet a red; add one only when there is genuinely nothing to do.

| Pattern | Reason |
|---|---|
| `D-MERGE-GLOBAL-INITFUNC` | Cycle 25 Stage B code-internal INVARIANT pin (`src/mir/merge/mir_merge.cpp`), NOT deferred work. Cited in the fail-loud abort that fires if a merged global's `initFunc` MirFuncId was not cloned into the merged module (`plan.funcMerged` miss). The invariant always holds for valid input — a global's module-init function is a defined function in the same CU, which the merge always clones (an init function is never a cross-CU weak loser). The abort is defense-in-depth: a breach means the planning pass dropped a function a global still references (a structural contradiction), so failing loud beats emitting a global whose initializer points at a stale/absent func. No closing work — it is a permanent guard, like the other `mergeFatal` invariant aborts. |

The contract they witness — the unsuppressable gate bypasses SILENCING (`--suppress` plus severity overrides) but must NOT bypass ELEVATION (`warningsAsErrors`) — is additionally pinned format-INDEPENDENTLY at the policy layer by `tests/core/test_unsuppressable_codes.cpp` (`UnsuppressableHonorsWarningsAsErrorsEvenWhenSuppressed`, plus the two silencing-bypass pins on the same code). It pins the two boundaries the fixture must NOT cross incidentally: all 513 externs share libSystem, so `libOrdinal` stays 1 and never approaches the 127 ceiling, and the symbols pool stays far under 8 MiB, so it never trips the name_offset overflow guard instead. ★ THE POINT IS THE FAILURE MODE IT PREVENTS: without the invariant, a later fixture edit — a second dylib, longer symbol names — would silently RE-ROUTE the test onto a different rejection surface while still going green, so the test would keep passing for the wrong reason and the multi-page guard would go unwitnessed.
